findings.title: InteriorPoint returns .optimal on an infeasible LP (violation 0.5) and overrides its own crossover's .infeasible verdict
findings.claim: README 2.5 InteriorPoint row ('Answers .infeasibleOrUnbounded when it cannot tell the two apart'); README 4 Limits 'Results' ('Optimal ... feasible and dual feasible to 1e-7'); Sources/ZTronLPCore/Solve/Status.swift:5 (.optimal: 'An optimal solution was found and proven').
findings.observed: min x+y s.t. x+y = 1e8, x+y = 1e8+1, x,y >= 0 (infeasible by 1). InteriorPoint() -> .optimal, objective 100000000.49999917, x = (50000000.25, 50000000.25), each row violated by 0.5. The same with crossover .none, presolve on or off, after an MPS write/read round trip, and through Conditioned(InteriorPoint()). With crossover .lite the crossover itself ends .infeasible and the strategy still returns .optimal, adding the warning 'crossover-lite ended with infeasible; returning the interior solution'. Simplex(.dual) and Automatic() -> .infeasible. Also B=1e6, delta=1e-2 (violation 5e-3) and an inequality variant (x+2y <= B, x+2y >= B+delta) with violation 0.77. Portfolio([Simplex(.dual), InteriorPoint()]) answered .infeasible 40/40 because the simplex won.

The package's own simplex, run inside the same solve, proved infeasibility, and that verdict was replaced by a success status.

findings.title: InteriorPoint returns .feasible(stoppedBy: .timeLimit) when a limit lands in the stalled path's crossover
findings.claim: README 2.5 InteriorPoint row: 'It never returns .feasible: a limit or a cancellation gives .noSolution.'
findings.observed: The model is 68x908 (a Hilbert-8 equality block plus a 30x30 assignment with tied costs). Unlimited, it stalls at 1.1 ms and the crossover finishes (141 pivots, optimal 12.606). With SolveContext.timeLimit 1.9..2.5 ms, 10 of 31 runs return .feasible(stoppedBy: .timeLimit) at objective 20.606 with a feasible point (violation 9e-10). Limits that land in the IPM give .noSolution(timeLimit). Cancellation at the stall gives .noSolution(cancelled), 5/5.
findings.whyWrong: The documented contract excludes .feasible for this strategy, so code written against it meets a status the docs say cannot occur. The point is feasible but not optimal.

findings.title: Presolved final bases (IPM crossover and simplex) are not optimal when a singleton row pins a column at its own bound
findings.claim: InteriorPoint.Crossover.lite doc ('return a vertex with its basis'); InteriorPointAnalysis.crossover doc ('its basis is what branch and bound reuses'); SimplexAnalysis.basis ('Reusable as WarmStart.basis'); README 2.2 (postsolve maps a basis back).
findings.observed: In instance k=56 of 'kkt 60 7 60 120' (28x22), row 13 is 2.737*x18 <= 0 with x18 >= 0. Presolve removes the row and fixes x18 = 0. The reported d18 is +7.94 and dual(row 13) is 0. InteriorPoint().finalBasis has x18 basic and row 13's logical atUpper. With x18 basic, y13 must be +2.9 on an at-upper <= row, which is the wrong sign. The basis vertex equals the returned x to 1e-14 but is dual infeasible by 2.9..77. Warm primal and dual simplex from it need 1..5 pivots on 4/60 instances, while every no-presolve basis needs 0. Simplex(.dual) and Simplex(.primal) with presolve return the same bases (shared cause).
findings.whyWrong: A basis returned as the optimal basis of the returned vertex must be dual feasible. This one is not, so warm starts and branch-and-bound reuse start from a non-optimal basis, and anything that reads it as an optimality certificate is misled.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/Model/Presolve.swift:432-448 (expandBasis, singletonRow case: when the column is at the tightened bound or .fixed it is made basic and the row's logical nonbasic, without consulting the reduced cost's sign)

findings.title: The interior-point tests cannot catch A3-01, A3-02, A3-03, A3-05 or A3-06
findings.claim: Tests as claims: IllConditionedTests.theInteriorPointDoesNotMistakeAStallForInfeasibility ('without it the result is a numerical failure that says what happened'); InteriorPointTests.infeasibleAndUnboundedAreReportedWithoutLooping; NetlibInteriorPointTests.convergesWithinFortyIterations.
findings.observed: (1) IllConditionedTests.swift:145-146 accepts .optimal from InteriorPoint(crossover: .none) without checking the point, so A3-06's 0.2..0.4 distances pass. (2) Every IllConditioned test uses only the Hilbert family with rhs = H*1 and unit-scale costs, so A3-02 (random condition 1e8..1e10) and A3-03 (scaled costs, free columns) are never exercised. (3) InteriorPointTests.swift:168 accepts .noSolution(.iterationLimit) and .infeasible. At :169, 'iterations <= 200' is vacuous because 200 is the default maxIterations, so a run to the cap passes. No test uses an infeasible model with a large rhs (A3-01). (4) InteriorPointTests.swift:42 allows a violation of 1e-5*(1+|obj|) against the README's 1e-7 (A3-05).
findings.whyWrong: Each test names a property it does not check: the documented failure mode can occur and the test still passes.
findings.repro: Read the cited lines. The behaviours they let through are reproduced by the A3-01, A3-02, A3-03, A3-05 and A3-06 repros. The tests themselves were not run.

findings.title: Defect 7 understates: the interior point itself never returns .infeasible or .unbounded
findings.claim: README 4 defect 7: 'it answers .infeasibleOrUnbounded for some models'.
findings.observed: 60 infeasible and 60 unbounded constructed models x 4 configurations (lite/none x presolve on/off), plus 3 textbook models. Unbounded 60/60 and textbook -> .infeasibleOrUnbounded. Infeasible 59/60 -> .infeasibleOrUnbounded and 1/60 -> .noSolution(.iterationLimit) after 200 iterations (mu 4e-8, primal residual 8e-3). Never .infeasible or .unbounded and never a certificate; only presolve or the stall->simplex path ever decides.
findings.whyWrong: 'For some models' implies the method usually tells the two apart. It never does: the worker has no other failure outcome.

summary: F3 holds on its main path. Constructed LPs (240/240 KKT-correct), netlib (13/13, iteration and pivot counts as in README 5), dense columns, analyzer estimates, thresholds and memory cap, and Conditioned's pass-through are all as documented.
